A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work with the same title and authors. All 17 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations and Appendix A, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original discounted-versus-undiscounted GRPO experiments, mathematical reasoning benchmark results in Tables 1–2, and a discount-factor sensitivity experiment.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original GRPO benchmark results in Tables 1–2 and the discount-factor experiment, now displayed in Figure 2.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same GRPO recipe: reasoning-length discounting of correctness rewards, undiscounted formatting rewards, reasoning-token masking and KL regularization against a moving reference. Equations (1)–(2) express the same objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K, MATH and a DeepScaleR training subset, with AMC 2023, AIME 2025, MINERVA and OLYMPIAD evaluation. The Qwen3 GSM8K sweep is also retained. The new theoretical MDP example does not add evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 compare discounted and undiscounted GRPO for the same model/dataset groups. The VERL and Roux et al. benchmarking passages remain. Added or removed related-work citations do not change the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Both versions retain greedy decoding at temperature zero, Pass@1 and mean response length, comparable token budgets, and training-accuracy-based discount selection. Completion limits remain 786, 2048 and 4096 tokens, with 1536 for the Qwen3 discount sweep.

E4.justification: The Qwen3 1.7B discount sensitivity experiment and the observation that whole-response discounting hurts GSM8K accuracy remain unchanged. V2's three-policy MDP is a formal illustration with a proof, rather than an added empirical ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Both versions report three training seeds and ten evaluation seeds for GSM8K/MATH, with evaluation seeds paired across methods, and five evaluation seeds for the other benchmarks. Averaging practices and uncertainty reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–2 are unchanged. For example, Qwen2.5 7B GSM8K retains Pass@1 of 91.06 versus 91.07 and lengths of 217.60 versus 170.08. The discount plot and reported 0.5–1.0% accuracy drop from whole-response discounting are also unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 permits stochastic transitions in the main setting and shortest-path theorem, formalizes terminal-verifier assumptions, adds Proposition 3.1/A.1 and its threshold proof, and defines a common critical discount for finite instance collections. The equality in v1 Theorems 3.10/A.14 becomes inclusion in v2 Theorems 3.6/A.16. The Taylor expansion and explicit discount-factor bound already existed in v1's appendix; their changed placement is not new theory. V2 Corollary A.17 nevertheless retains the stronger equality.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the framing from deterministic LRM reasoning to general goal-reaching and stochastic shortest-path problems. The conclusion likewise broadens the length-penalty claim to finite-horizon MDPs. The central accuracy-preserving shortening contribution and empirical claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds an interpretation of the Blackwell threshold as instance hardness: proximity to one requires more careful discount selection to avoid sacrificing success. It also explains a common discount across finite instance collections and foregrounds the success-first, conditional-length interpretation.

D1.justification: V1's first-page footnote provides the authors' implementation repository link; v2 removes it without a replacement elsewhere. This reduces documented code access, without establishing that the repository became unavailable. The training and inference implementation information otherwise remains.

R1.justification: V2 adds Haarnoja et al. (2018) to support softmax training with greedy deployment and removes Liu et al. (2025c) and She et al. (2025). It emphasizes stochastic shortest-path positioning while retaining the existing efficient-reasoning taxonomy and principal Blackwell references.

P1.justification: The theory narrative is substantially reorganized: language modeling becomes Section 2.1; Section 3 presents motivation, the Taylor expansion and shortest-path guarantee before existence results. Detailed time augmentation and the explicit bound remain in the appendix but leave the main text. Revised introductory prose, a roadmap and a proof sketch support this restructuring.

P2.justification: V2 adds the MDP schematic as Figure 1 and enlarges and relocates the unchanged discount plot as Figure 2. Table 2's caption is shortened, surrounding text reflows, and conference headers are added. The experimental table structures and plot axes remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 aligns Theorems 3.6/A.16 with the one-way implication actually proved, while the worked example and reordered exposition make the theory easier to assess. The improvement is limited because Corollary A.17 still asserts equality without resolving the converse, and the implementation link is removed. The empirical evidence remains unchanged.
